lines.text: The hundred-and-twentieth minute. The goal was open. The header was perfect. An entire continent rose to its feet...

And a hand reached out of nowhere and stole it. To this day, no African nation has ever reached a World Cup semifinal. One was closer than anyone — and in the stands tonight sits the boy who watched it happen.
Last time, we predicted England would edge Croatia two-one. Tonight: the cruellest near-miss in football... against the purest first dream.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends, episode twenty-six. Ghana versus Panama. The Black Stars... against Los Canaleros.
And stay with me — because both of these nations have lived a World Cup story you will never forget.
First, the history. And it is true. South Africa, twenty-ten. Ghana, against Uruguay, for a place in the semifinals.
The last kick of extra time. One-one. Ghana send a header goalward — and Luis Suarez punches it off the line with both hands.
He is sent off. A penalty, to win it, for all of Africa. Asamoah Gyan steps up... and strikes the crossbar.
Ghana lose the shootout. No African team has ever come closer. It is the cruellest near-miss the game has known.
Yet Ghana are giants. The first nation ever to win four African titles. Gyan, the highest-scoring African in World Cup history.
And across from them — Panama. Los Canaleros. For most of their history, a nation that had never tasted a World Cup at all.
Until one night in twenty seventeen rewrote everything they believed was possible.
The final qualifier. Costa Rica. The eighty-eighth minute. And up climbs a defender, Roman Torres, to smash in the goal that changed a country.
Panama reach their first ever World Cup — and the United States are knocked out. The President declares the next day a national holiday.
And in Russia, Felipe Baloy, thirty-seven years old, scores Panama's first ever World Cup goal — and they celebrate it like a final.
Now, Ghana. Jordan Ayew captains them — relentless, clever, at his third World Cup.
Antoine Semenyo brings the power. Inaki Williams brings the pace. Thomas Partey holds the engine room.
Four-time African champions, chasing the semifinal that history still owes them.
But Panama have a spine of steel. Adalberto Carrasquilla — Coco — pulls the strings in midfield.
Michael Murillo flies down the right. Cecilio Waterman hunts the goal. And captain Anibal Godoy has worn the shirt more than anyone alive.
So here is the duel. Ghanaian pace and pedigree... against the grit of a nation that knows how to make history out of nothing.
Our prediction — built on Ghana's cutting edge, on a continent still waiting, and on a Panama side that never, ever stops fighting. Watch.
Ghana surge early. Williams runs in behind, squares it — and Semenyo finishes. One-nil, Black Stars.
But you do not tell Los Canaleros it's over. Carrasquilla feeds Waterman, and the striker buries it. One-all. Panama roar.
Then Ghana's class arrives. A break, a cross, and the captain Jordan Ayew is there to win it. Two-one.
Two-one at the whistle, in our story. Ghana edge it — but Panama walk off heads high. They belonged.
Do you agree? Comment BLACK STARS if Ghana's quality is too much. Comment CANALEROS if you back Panama to shock them.
And that boy in the stands? Legend number twenty-six: the Boy from Soccer City. He saw the penalty hit the bar... and he never stopped believing.
Sixteen years he carried that night. Tonight he came back for the ending Africa was denied. Collect him inside the game.
Which brings us to YOU. At WorldCup twenty-six dot world, pick three of the forty-eight nations — and every goal they score scores for you.
Free to play. Climb the leaderboard, just for fun. No prizes. Hit like, send this to a friend, and subscribe — the legends are only beginning.
